// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zOpt\zOpt.cpp -- zOpt::EvalIntCompareOp.
//
// int __fastcall EvalIntCompareOp(const char* opString /*ecx*/, int lhs /*edx*/, int rhs /*stack+4*/);
// Caller: zOpt::EvaluateProfileMetricCondition @ 0x4074eb, 0x407539, 0x407587, 0x4075d5, 0x407629.
//
// Evaluates "lhs <opString> rhs" for an integer-valued metric/condition node and
// returns 1 if true, 0 otherwise. opString is the 2-char ASCII operator parsed from
// the .zrdr OPT condition (e.g. "==", "<", ">", "<=", ">=", "!=", "~=").
//
// Dispatch pattern (7 open-coded strcmp chains, then 7 setcc returns):
//   1. strcmp(opString, "==")  @ 0x4da654 (g_zOpt_OpStr_Eq)   -> sete  cl ; return (lhs==rhs)
//   2. strcmp(opString, "<")   @ 0x4da650 (g_zOpt_OpStr_Lt)   -> setl  cl ; return (lhs s<  rhs)
//   3. strcmp(opString, ">")   @ 0x4da64c (g_zOpt_OpStr_Gt)   -> setg  cl ; return (lhs s>  rhs)
//   4. strcmp(opString, "<=")  @ 0x4da648 (g_zOpt_OpStr_Le)   -> setle cl ; return (lhs s<= rhs)
//   5. strcmp(opString, ">=")  @ 0x4da644 (g_zOpt_OpStr_Ge)   -> setge cl ; return (lhs s>= rhs)
//   6. strcmp(opString, "!=")  @ 0x4da640 (g_zOpt_OpStr_Ne)   -> setne cl ; return (lhs !=  rhs)
//   7. strcmp(opString, "~=")  @ 0x4da63c (g_zOpt_OpStr_TolEq) -> tolerance-equality (see below)
// Unknown opString falls through all 7 tests and returns 0.
//
// The "~=" branch is tolerance-equality: returns 1 iff |lhs - rhs| < lhs * g_zOpt_CompareTolerancePct
// (= 0.02 @ 0x4ccd98, i.e. "within 2 percent of lhs"). Operands are loaded via fild as signed
// int32, then compared with fcompp; the "test ah, 0x41 / jne" pattern is the MSVC "ST0 > ST1"
// short-circuit (if neither C0 nor C3 is set, ST0 is strictly greater than ST1).
//
// Absolute value formula at 0x407425-0x40742c: cdq produces edx = (eax>>31), then
// eax = (eax ^ edx) - edx  == |eax|, writing it back to [esp+0x18] for fild.
//
// Variable mapping: cursorXx is the per-branch strcmp cursor into opString; patternXx is the
// per-branch cursor into g_zOpt_OpStr_Xx.  esi_N/ecx_13 are the post-loop sbb-based "strcmp
// delta" results that test as 0 on match (esi_1=Eq, esi_3=Lt, esi_5=Gt, esi_7=Le, esi_9=Ge,
// esi_11=Ne, ecx_13=TolEq). lhsSpillSlot (@[esp+0x10]) starts as a spill of ecx (opString)
// then is overwritten with edx (lhs) at 0x407225 -- the "~=" branch reads it back via fild.
//
// EXHAUSTION (criterion 11 -- BN limitation basis):
//   * 7x `sbb esi, esi; sbb esi, 0xffffffff` after each strcmp loop renders as
//     `unimplemented {sbb esi, esi}` plus two nested sbb.d() calls -- this is the MSVC open-
//     coded "strcmp delta" (sets esi to -1/0/+1 based on carry after the per-char mismatch).
//     BN's HLIL has no strcmp recognizer and cannot fold this back into a clean `strcmp(a,b)`
//     call form. Attempted: (a) split-variable at sbb sink and retype to int (didn't help --
//     BN still rendered the sbb chain); (b) retype esi_* sequence to int32_t (same); (c)
//     rewrite the flag variables c_* (flag lifetimes are BN-internal). Accepted as ☑️ limit.
//   * The 7 pattern/cursor SSA splits (register-varN) are functionally identical per branch;
//     BN re-splits them every time a prototype is changed, so names drift by 1-2 branches
//     after re-analysis. Verified current state: cursor*/pattern* pairs align with the

// For each i in [0, 23):

// Likely original file: D:\Proj\Battlesport\hud.cpp
//
// The sensor auxiliary overlay uses g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[23]. This __fastcall helper selects one of three line operations by op:
//
// op == 1: SetTextFmt(format), then SetVisible(1).
// op == 0: SetVisible(0), ignoring format.
// op == 2: if *format is non-empty, SetTextFmt(format) and SetVisible(1); otherwise SetVisible(0).
//
// Called by HudUiAuxOverlay::ClearTextLines and sensor/debug overlay handlers.
0x4137f0 void __fastcall HudUiAuxOverlay::ApplyTextLineOp(int32_t op, int32_t index, char const* format)
{
    if (op == 1)
        struct HudUiStringMenu* stringMenu = g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu
        stringMenu->items[index].vtbl->SetTextFmt(&stringMenu->items[index], format)
        g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[index].vtbl->SetVisible(1)
        return

    if (op == 0)
        g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[index].vtbl->SetVisible(0)
        return

    if (op != 2)
        return

    if (*format != 0)
        struct HudUiPanelCore* textLine = &g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[index]
        textLine->vtbl->SetTextFmt(textLine, format)
        g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[index].vtbl->SetVisible(1)
        return

    g_HudUiMgr.sensor.stringMenu->items[index].vtbl->SetVisible(0)
}

// Source file: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zReader\zReader.cpp
//
// Given a zReader-locatable filename (relative, bare, or search-path-relative), builds the absolute parent directory — "{drive}{dir}" — into `outParentDir`.
//
// Pipeline:
//   1. zReader::TryResolvePath(filename, NULL) — resolve via direct exists test then g_zRdr_SearchPathList fallback.
//   2. _fullpath(buf[0x104], resolved, 0x104) — expand to absolute path, resolve "." and "..".
//   3. _splitpath(buf, drive[3], dir[0x100], filename[0x100], ext[0x100]) — CRT path decomposition. Only drive + dir are retained; filename/ext are computed into locals purely to satisfy the _splitpath contract.
//   4. sprintf(outParentDir, "%s%s", drive, dir) — concatenate drive letter (e.g. "D:") with directory path (e.g. "\Proj\Game\levels\") to produce "D:\Proj\Game\levels\".
//
// outParentDir must have room for at least 0x103 bytes (drive + MAX_PATH-ish dir + trailing '\0'). Caller-owned buffer.
//
// Format string literal at 0x4dc6c8 is "%s%s". Note the output DOES retain the trailing path separator from _splitpath's dir segment.
//
// Return is void in source; typed int32_t per AGENTS.md policy for eax tracking.
0x421e20 int32_t __fastcall zReader::BuildResolvedParentDir(char const* filename, char* outParentDir)
{
    char _FullPath[0x104]
    _fullpath(&_FullPath, zReader::TryResolvePath(filename, nullptr), 0x104)
    char _Drive[0x3]
    char _Dir[0x100]
    char _Ext[0x100]
    char _Filename[0x100]
    _splitpath(&_FullPath, &_Drive, &_Dir, &_Filename, &_Ext)
    // Exhaustion attempts for `return sprintf(...)` BN artifact (crit 11 ☑️):
    //   1. Function declared int32_t return (AGENTS.md policy to preserve eax tracking).
    //   2. BN renders the last eax-producing call as `return <call>`. Source is void — sprintf's return value (char count written) is unused by callers.
    //   3. Attempted setting explicit void-return prototype — violates AGENTS.md policy and caused cascade regressions in prior sessions.
    //   4. Cannot suppress the `return ...` synthesis while keeping int32_t return — BN's HLIL policy chooses the last eax-live expression.
    //   5. Documented at function-level comment; accepted as the int32_t-return-policy trade-off.
    return sprintf(outParentDir, "%s%s", &_Drive, &_Dir)
}

// Likely source: src/Battlesport/player.cpp
// For the local active player, iterates the pickup pending-contact queue and calls Pickup::OnCollected for contacts whose collection raycast is unobstructed.
0x424210 void __fastcall Player::ProcessPendingPickupContacts(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState

    if (saveState != g_GameStateOrMapTable)
        return

    enum PlayerLifecycleState state = playerState->lifecycle.state

    if (state == PLAYER_LIFECYCLE_INACTIVE || state == PLAYER_LIFECYCLE_DESTROYED)
        return

    struct PlayerPendingContact* contact = playerState->pickupQueue.head

    while (contact != 0)
        if (PlayerPickupContact::PassesCollectionTest(saveState, contact) != 0)

        if (contact == 0)
            contact = nullptr
        else
            contact = contact->next
}

    playerState->transformedPos.y = playerState->worldPos.y
    playerState->transformedPos.x = playerState->worldPos.x
    playerState->transformedPos.z = playerState->worldPos.z
    Player::RebuildSteerBasisFromMotionBasis(saveState)
    long double verticalVelocityAfterGravity = playerState->projectileSpawnVel.y - playerState->gravityAccel * g_Player_DeltaTime
    playerState->projectileSpawnVel.y = verticalVelocityAfterGravity
    long double advancedWorldPosY = verticalVelocityAfterGravity * g_Player_DeltaTime + playerState->worldPos.y
    playerState->worldPos.y = advancedWorldPosY
    playerState->transformedPos.y = advancedWorldPosY
    Player::BuildEnvironmentProbeResult(saveState, &probeResult)
    int32_t eax_1
    int80_t st0_2
    eax_1, st0_2 = Player::ApplyEnvironmentProbeResult(saveState, &probeResult)

    if (eax_1 == 0)
        return

    Player::ProcessEnvProbeResults(saveState, &probeResult)
    Player::RebuildOrientationFromNormal(saveState)

    if (saveState == g_GameStateOrMapTable && playerState->airborneFlag == 0)
        Player::FindThirdProbeAndComputeNormal(saveState, &probeResult)

    Player::UpdateVerticalVelocityAndTransform(saveState, &probeResult)
}

// Source file: D:\Proj\Battlesport\player.cpp
//
// Matrix layout (all 3x4 row-major, 12 floats each):
//   local gunMatrix = gunNode local matrix
//   local turretMatrix = turretNode local matrix (yaw-only: middle row/col = identity)
//   local gunFireTransform = playerState->gunFireTransform
// Output outMatrix34[0..8] = 3x3 rotation product; outMatrix34[9..11] = playerState->aimBasisOrigin.
// BN artifact: the x87 operand-cache sequence still renders as scattered long-double temporaries even after the zMat4x3 overlays.
0x43afd0 void __fastcall Player::ComposeAimBasisWorldMatrix(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState, struct zMat4x3* outMatrix34)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState
    struct zMat4x3 gunMatrix
    __builtin_memcpy(&gunMatrix, zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DGetMatrixPtr(playerState->gunNode), 0x30)
    struct zMat4x3 turretMatrix
    __builtin_memcpy(&turretMatrix, zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DGetMatrixPtr(playerState->turretNode), 0x30)
    // Pre-load FPU stack with 6 copies of turret[6] and turret[8] (third row of yaw-only rotation), then turret[0]. This front-loads the operand cache so later fxch/faddp sequences can reuse them for multiple output rows without reloading from memory. BN's decomp renders this as scattered `var_60` / `var_58` references.
    long double x87_r7 = turretMatrix.zx
    long double x87_r6 = turretMatrix.zz
    long double x87_r5 = turretMatrix.zx
    long double x87_r4 = turretMatrix.zz
    long double x87_r3 = turretMatrix.zx
    long double x87_r2 = turretMatrix.zz
    long double x87_r1 = turretMatrix.xx
    struct zMat4x3 gunFireTransform
    __builtin_memcpy(&gunFireTransform, &playerState->gunFireTransform, 0x30)
    outMatrix34->xx = x87_r1 * gunFireTransform.xx + turretMatrix.xz * gunFireTransform.zx
    outMatrix34->xy = turretMatrix.xx * gunFireTransform.xy + turretMatrix.xz * gunFireTransform.zy
    outMatrix34->xz = turretMatrix.xx * gunFireTransform.xz + turretMatrix.xz * gunFireTransform.zz
    float var_94 = x87_r7 * gunFireTransform.xx + x87_r6 * gunFireTransform.zx
    long double x87_r3_2 = x87_r5 * gunFireTransform.xy
    long double x87_r1_12 = gunFireTransform.yy
    outMatrix34->yx = gunFireTransform.yx * gunMatrix.yy + gunMatrix.yz * var_94
    long double x87_r2_10 = gunFireTransform.yz
    float var_98 = x87_r3_2 + x87_r4 * gunFireTransform.zy
    long double x87_r2_12 = gunMatrix.yz
    long double x87_r3_12 = x87_r3 * gunFireTransform.xz
    long double x87_r2_14 = gunFireTransform.yx
    outMatrix34->yy = x87_r1_12 * gunMatrix.yy + gunMatrix.yz * var_98
    float var_9c = x87_r3_12 + x87_r2 * gunFireTransform.zz
    long double x87_r4_8 = x87_r2_14 * gunMatrix.zy
    long double x87_r5_4 = gunMatrix.zz * var_94
    outMatrix34->yz = x87_r2_10 * gunMatrix.yy + x87_r2_12 * var_9c
    outMatrix34->zx = x87_r4_8 + x87_r5_4
    long double x87_r4_16 = gunFireTransform.yz * gunMatrix.zy
    long double x87_r5_10 = gunMatrix.zz * var_9c
    outMatrix34->zy = gunFireTransform.yy * gunMatrix.zy + gunMatrix.zz * var_98
    outMatrix34->zz = x87_r4_16 + x87_r5_10
    // Translation part of output: copies playerState->aimBasisOrigin.{x,y,z} (at playerState+0xEB4..0xEBC) into outMatrix[9..11]. The aim-basis pos is set elsewhere (see ClearGunFireSlotsAndApplyOffsets fallback path at 0x43ac83 which writes playerState+0xEB4).
    outMatrix34->posX = playerState->aimBasisOrigin.x
    outMatrix34->posY = playerState->aimBasisOrigin.y
    outMatrix34->posZ = playerState->aimBasisOrigin.z

    // [comments not attached to rendered lines]
    // [comment @ 0x43b03e]
    // Row0 of output rotation: out[0..2] = turret[0][*] * gunFire[*][0..2]. Because turret is yaw-only (middle row/col = identity), out[0][0] collapses to turret[0][0]*gunFire[0][0] + turret[0][2]*gunFire[2][0] -- the turret[0][1]*gunFire[1][0] middle term is elided at compile time.
}

// Likely source: src/Battlesport/player.cpp
// Builds PlayerState::gunFireTransform from the root node Object3D matrix and the current modal node Object3D matrix. If the modal node is absent, the root matrix is copied directly.
// BN limitation: the x87 float arithmetic still renders with fconvert.s/fconvert.t around the field-typed unrolled matrix combine.
0x43b1b0 void __fastcall Player::BuildGunFireTransform(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState
    struct PlayerModalState* primaryModalState = saveState->primaryModalState
    struct zMat4x3* eax = zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DGetMatrixPtr(playerState->rootNode)
    struct zMat4x3 rootMatrix
    __builtin_memcpy(&rootMatrix, eax, 0x30)
    struct zClass_Node* node = primaryModalState->modalNode

    if (node == 0)
        __builtin_memcpy(&playerState->gunFireTransform, eax, 0x30)
        return

    struct zMat4x3 modalMatrix
    __builtin_memcpy(&modalMatrix, zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DGetMatrixPtr(node), 0x30)
    playerState->gunFireTransform.xx = modalMatrix.xx * rootMatrix.xx + modalMatrix.xy * rootMatrix.yx + modalMatrix.xz * rootMatrix.zx
    playerState->gunFireTransform.xy = modalMatrix.xx * rootMatrix.xy + modalMatrix.xy * rootMatrix.yy + modalMatrix.xz * rootMatrix.zy
    playerState->gunFireTransform.xz = modalMatrix.xx * rootMatrix.xz + modalMatrix.xy * rootMatrix.yz + modalMatrix.xz * rootMatrix.zz
    playerState->gunFireTransform.yx = modalMatrix.yx * rootMatrix.xx + modalMatrix.yy * rootMatrix.yx + modalMatrix.yz * rootMatrix.zx
    playerState->gunFireTransform.yy = modalMatrix.yx * rootMatrix.xy + modalMatrix.yy * rootMatrix.yy + modalMatrix.yz * rootMatrix.zy
    playerState->gunFireTransform.yz = modalMatrix.yx * rootMatrix.xz + modalMatrix.yy * rootMatrix.yz + modalMatrix.yz * rootMatrix.zz
    playerState->gunFireTransform.zx = modalMatrix.zy * rootMatrix.yx + modalMatrix.zz * rootMatrix.zx
    playerState->gunFireTransform.zy = modalMatrix.zy * rootMatrix.yy + modalMatrix.zz * rootMatrix.zy
    playerState->gunFireTransform.posX = modalMatrix.posY * rootMatrix.yx + modalMatrix.posZ * rootMatrix.zx + rootMatrix.posX
    playerState->gunFireTransform.zz = modalMatrix.zy * rootMatrix.yz + modalMatrix.zz * rootMatrix.zz
    playerState->gunFireTransform.posY = modalMatrix.posY * rootMatrix.yy + modalMatrix.posZ * rootMatrix.zy + rootMatrix.posY
    playerState->gunFireTransform.posZ = modalMatrix.posY * rootMatrix.yz + modalMatrix.posZ * rootMatrix.zz + rootMatrix.posZ
}

// Likely source: src/Battlesport/player.cpp
// Applies a desired pitch/Y component to an in-place aim direction. Assembly computes horizontalLenSq = direction->x^2 + direction->z^2; if nonzero it rescales X/Z by sqrt((1 - pitchY^2) / horizontalLenSq) using the retail fast float-bit approximation, then writes direction->y = pitchY. If the horizontal direction is zero, pitchY == 0 falls back to the default alt-gun aim direction (0, 0, -1); otherwise X/Z are seeded to the diagonal sqrt((1 - pitchY^2) * 0.5) approximation.
// BN limitation: the x87 stack and float-bit sqrt approximation render as fconvert/s>> temporaries and obscure the direction->x^2 + direction->z^2 sum in HLIL.
0x43b500 void __thiscall Player::ApplyAimPitchToDirection(struct zVec3* direction, float pitchY)

    long double x87_r6 = direction->x
    long double temp1 = 0f
    x87_r6 - temp1

    if ((((x87_r6 < temp1 ? 1 : 0) << 8 | (is_unordered.t(x87_r6, temp1) ? 1 : 0) << 0xa | (x87_r6 == temp1 ? 1 : 0) << 0xe | 0x3800):1.b & 0x40) == 0)
        long double x87_r7_10 = ((1f - pitchY * pitchY) / x87_r6 s>> 1) + 0x1fc00000 * direction->x
        direction->y = pitchY
        direction->x = x87_r7_10
        direction->z = ((1f - pitchY * pitchY) / x87_r6 s>> 1) + 0x1fc00000 * direction->z
        return

    long double x87_r7_4 = pitchY
    long double temp2 = 0f
    x87_r7_4 - temp2

    if ((((x87_r7_4 < temp2 ? 1 : 0) << 8 | (is_unordered.t(x87_r7_4, temp2) ? 1 : 0) << 0xa | (x87_r7_4 == temp2 ? 1 : 0) << 0xe):1.b & 0x40) == 0)
        direction->z = ((1f - pitchY * pitchY) * 0.5f s>> 1) + 0x1fc00000
        direction->x = ((1f - pitchY * pitchY) * 0.5f s>> 1) + 0x1fc00000
        direction->y = pitchY
        return

    direction->x = g_Player_AltGunAimOriginDefaultX
    direction->y = g_Player_AltGunAimOriginDefaultY
    direction->z = g_Player_AltGunAimOriginDefaultZ
}

// Source: zWeapon.cpp -- Player::UpdateAltGunFireController.
//
// Continuous/beam alt-gun tick helper. If the current master type is SUB, queues fixed damage and exits. 0x43c2d0 void __fastcall Player::UpdateContinuousAltGunFireController(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState
    struct PlayerGunFireController* activeAltGunController = playerState->activeAltGunController

    if (saveState->primaryModalState->masterModalData->masterType == PLAYER_MASTER_TYPE_SUB)
        playerState->queuedFixedDamageFlag = 1
        return

        g_HudSensorTracker.missionStat2 += 1

    if (edi_5 s>= 0xa)
        return

    while (true)
        struct PlayerAltWeaponBankControllerScanView* esi

        if ((esi->ctrlA.flags.b & 4) != 0 && Player::IsAltWeaponAllowedInCurrentMasterMode(saveState, esi->ctrlA.optCatalogEntry) != 0)
            long double x87_r7_4 = esi->ctrlA.ammoOrCharge
            long double temp2_1 = 0f
            x87_r7_4 - temp2_1
            int32_t eax_20
            eax_20.w = (x87_r7_4 < temp2_1 ? 1 : 0) << 8 | (is_unordered.t(x87_r7_4, temp2_1) ? 1 : 0) << 0xa | (x87_r7_4 == temp2_1 ? 1 : 0) << 0xe

            if ((eax_20:1.b & 0x41) == 0)
                Player::HandleAltWeaponBankSelectInput(edi_5 + 0xe)
                break
                break

        if ((esi->ctrlB.flags.b & 4) != 0 && Player::IsAltWeaponAllowedInCurrentMasterMode(saveState, esi->ctrlB.optCatalogEntry) != 0)
            long double x87_r7_5 = esi->ctrlB.ammoOrCharge
            long double temp4_1 = 0f
            x87_r7_5 - temp4_1

            if ((((x87_r7_5 < temp4_1 ? 1 : 0) << 8 | (is_unordered.t(x87_r7_5, temp4_1) ? 1 : 0) << 0xa | (x87_r7_5 == temp4_1 ? 1 : 0) << 0xe):1.b & 0x41) == 0)
                Player::HandleAltWeaponBankSelectInput(edi_5 + 0xe)
                break

        edi_5 += 1
        esi = &esi[1]

        if (edi_5 s>= 0xa)
    // No-weapon-found fallthrough: upward loop exhausted without a hit. Returns last eax_14 (comparison flags); callers ignore the value.
            return
}

// Likely source: src/Battlesport/player.cpp
// Tears down the active alt-gun trail/projectile runtime, resets door and timed-hit state, returns the alt-gun transition state to idle, and hides/restores attach-node transforms for weapon banks 2..9. PlayerAltWeaponBankAttachResetCursorView models BN's subobject loop cursor at altWeaponBanks[2].controllers[0].attachNodePrimary; the assembly advances by the 0xac bank stride.
0x43c850 void __fastcall Player::ResetAltGunRuntimeState(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState
    struct PlayerGunFireController* activeAltGunController = playerState->activeAltGunController

    if (playerState->altGunFireHeldFlag != 0)
    // Clear altGunFireHeldFlag (+0x5BC) and deactivate the trail runtime on the
    // active controller (ctrl->trailRuntimeState at offset 0x50). This block is gated
    // on altGunFireHeldFlag != 0 — when the player isn't currently holding fire, skip
    // the trail cleanup entirely (no live trail to tear down).
        playerState->altGunFireHeldFlag = 0
        OptCatalog::DeactivateTrailRuntimeState(activeAltGunController->trailRuntimeState)

    struct OptCatalogRuntimeInstance* attachState = activeAltGunController->attachState

    if (attachState != 0)
        zClass_Class::RemoveChild(activeAltGunController->attachNodePrimary, attachState->projectileNode)
        OptCatalog::RecycleRuntimeInstanceStorage(activeAltGunController->optCatalogEntry, activeAltGunController->attachState)
        activeAltGunController->attachState = nullptr

    // Player::ResetAltGunDoorAnimationState(saveState) — clears altGunTransitionTimerB
    // and restores doorLeftNode/doorRightNode scale to (1,1,1). Thiscall: ecx = ebx
    // (the saveState this-pointer we entered with).
    Player::ResetAltGunDoorAnimationState(saveState)
    PlayerTimedHitStatus::ClearLightAndReset(&playerState->timedHitStatus)
    // Reset the alt-gun transition state machine:
    //   [esi+0x5e0] altGunTransitionState = 1  (idle, ready-to-select-new-weapon)
    //   [esi+0xf20] altGunTransitionController = null
    //   [esi+0xf28] altGunTransitionTimerA = 0.0f (ebp == 0 from xor at 0x43c858)
    // Matches the initial state Player::TickAltGunRuntimeState expects at case 0.
    playerState->altGunTransitionState = 1
    playerState->altGunTransitionController = nullptr
    playerState->altGunTransitionTimerA = 0f
    // Set up bank-reset loop:
    //   add esi, 0x754  — advance from PlayerState base to
    //                     altWeaponBanks[2].ctrlA.attachNodePrimary_0c
    //                     (altWeaponBanks base 0x5EC + 2*0xAC + 0x10 = 0x754).
    //   mov edi, 8      — iteration count; loop visits banks 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9.
    // Banks 0 (unarmed) and 1 (aux-effect) are intentionally skipped: neither
    // maintains a scene-graph attach node that needs resetting.
    struct PlayerAltWeaponBankAttachResetCursorView* bankAttachResetCursor = &playerState->altWeaponBanks[2].controllers[0].attachNodePrimary
    int32_t i_1 = 8
    int32_t i

    do
    // ctrlA side reset for current bank. esi points at ctrlA.attachNodePrimary_0c.
    // Field offsets within the *current* esi context:
    //   [esi+0x00] = ctrlA.attachNodePrimary_0c
    //   [esi+0x10] = ctrlA.attachPosX  (ctrlA+0x1C, ctrlA starts at bank+0x04)
    //   [esi+0x14] = ctrlA.attachPosY  (ctrlA+0x20)
    //   [esi+0x18] = ctrlA.attachPosZ  (ctrlA+0x24)
    // If the attach-node pointer is null (rare — bank lacks a ctrlA mount), skip the
    // whole ctrlA reset block and jump to ctrlB at 0x43c901.
        struct zClass_Node* node = bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachNodePrimary

        if (node != 0)
    // gwNodeSetActive(node, 0) — hide the ctrlA weapon model. Second arg edx=0
    // from `xor edx, edx` — both a nullified active flag and the zeroed edx serving
    // as the "deactivate" selector.
            zClass_Class::gwNodeSetActive(node, 0)
    // gwObject3DSetPosition(node, posX, posY, posZ) — restore the weapon's local
    // position to its stored attach offset. The three pushes copy out attachPosX/Y/Z
    // loaded just above. Even though the node is deactivated, position is reset so
    // the next activation starts from a known transform.
            zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DSetPosition(bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachNodePrimary, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachPosX, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachPosY, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachPosZ)
    // gwObject3DSetScale(node, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) — three `push 0x3f800000` (=1.0f)
    // before the call. BN's HLIL renders this as `*(esp-N) = 0x3f800000`, but it's
    // just the standard cdecl float-arg push sequence.
            zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DSetScale(bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlA.attachNodePrimary, 1f, 1f, 1f)

    // ctrlB side reset for current bank. esi still points at ctrlA.attachNodePrimary_0c,
    // so ctrlB fields are offset by ctrlA size (0x54):
    //   [esi+0x54] = ctrlB.attachNodePrimary_0c  (ctrlA+0x54 = ctrlB+0x0C = bank+0x64)
    //   [esi+0x64] = ctrlB.attachPosX  (ctrlB+0x1C = bank+0x74)
    //   [esi+0x68] = ctrlB.attachPosY  (ctrlB+0x20)
    //   [esi+0x6c] = ctrlB.attachPosZ  (ctrlB+0x24)
    // Same null-skip pattern as ctrlA. If ctrlB is absent (single-mount weapon),
    // jumps past to the loop step at 0x43c93a.
        struct zClass_Node* node_1 = bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachNodePrimary

        if (node_1 != 0)
            zClass_Class::gwNodeSetActive(node_1, 0)
            zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DSetPosition(bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachNodePrimary, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachPosX, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachPosY, bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachPosZ)
            zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DSetScale(bankAttachResetCursor->ctrlB.attachNodePrimary, 1f, 1f, 1f)

    // Loop step: advance to next bank.
    //   add esi, 0xac   — PlayerAltWeaponBankRuntime stride is 0xAC (bank 2→3→...→9).
    //   dec edi         — iteration counter starts at 8.
    //   jne 0x43c8cb    — falls through to ret after 8 iterations (banks 2..9).
        bankAttachResetCursor = &bankAttachResetCursor[1]
        i = i_1
        i_1 -= 1
    while (i != 1)

    // [comments not attached to rendered lines]
    // [comment @ 0x43c880]
    // attachState_28 != null branch — there's a live projectile/attach runtime on the
    // active controller. Three-step cleanup:
    //  1. zClass_Class::RemoveChild(ctrl->attachNodePrimary_0c, attachState->projectileNode_0c)
    //     — detach the projectile from the weapon's attach node.
    //  2. OptCatalog_RecycleRuntimeInstanceStorage(ctrl->optCatalogEntry_00, ctrl->attachState_28)
    //     — return the runtime instance to the OptCatalog's pool.
    //  3. ctrl->attachState_28 = nullptr — clear the slot so we don't double-free.
    // Order matters: detach from scene graph before recycling storage.
    // [comment @ 0x43c89f]
    // lea ecx, [esi+0x5c4] — next call (PlayerTimedHitStatus_ClearLightAndReset) takes
    // a pointer to the embedded PlayerTimedHitStatus struct at PlayerState+0x5C4, NOT
    // an uninitialized stack value as BN's HLIL misrenders. Thiscall convention.
}

// Resolves a (saveState, weaponId) pair to the PlayerGunFireController* that owns
// that weapon id on this player. Used by netplay alt-gun replay to locate the
// matching controller on a remote player so the replay uses the correct
// optCatalogEntry, ammo slot, and attach state.
//
// Algorithm:
//  1. entry = OptCatalog_FindEntryById(weaponId)  — translate the wire-format
//     weapon id into the local OptCatalogEntryDef* pointer (may be null if the
//     weapon id isn't registered on this client).
//  2. Linear scan banks 2..9 (both sides): for each bank i in [2,9]:
//     - if altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlA.optCatalogEntry_00 == entry: return &ctrlA
//     - else if altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlB.optCatalogEntry_00 == entry: return &ctrlB
//  3. Fallback: return &altWeaponBanks[1].ctrlA (the primary-variant lane).
//     This is what remote dispatches resolve to when the weapon id isn't an
//     explicit alt-bank weapon — keeps the caller with a non-null controller
//     so it can still consume ammo / play sound even on mismatched remote state.
//
// Bank identities at runtime (confirmed via OptCatalog tables):
// - bank 1    = dedicated primary-variant lane (fallback target)
// - bank 4    = P_HEMINE / P_QMINE             (Phoenix mines)
// - bank 5    = R_HEMINE / R_QMINE             (Raptor mines)
// - bank 6    = LOCKON_LASER / LASER_SABRE
// - bank 7    = SONIC_CANNON / ARC_SABRE
// - bank 8    = MISSILE / GUIDED_MISSILE
// - bank 9    = NUKE / GUIDED_NUKE
// - banks 2,3 = ship-specific slots (varies per loadout)
//
// Offset math in the asm (derivations for the magic constants):
// - Loop cursor starts at [esi+0x79C] = altWeaponBanks[2].ctrlB.optCatalogEntry_00
//   (altWeaponBanks base 0x5EC + 2*0xAC + ctrlB offset 0x58 + optCatalogEntry 0x00 = 0x79C)
// - `[edx-0x54]` reads the same-bank ctrlA.optCatalogEntry (ctrlB→ctrlA offset = -0x54)
// - ctrlA return addr: esi + i*0xAC + 0x5F0  (= 0x5EC + i*0xAC + 0x04 = &bank[i].ctrlA)
// - ctrlB return addr: esi + i*0xAC + 0x644  (= 0x5EC + i*0xAC + 0x58 = &bank[i].ctrlB)
// - Both paths compute i*0xAC via: i*43 = (i*7)*3 + i → (shl 3, sub i, lea+lea+lea)
// - Fallback return addr: esi + 0x69C  (= 0x5EC + 1*0xAC + 0x04 = &bank[1].ctrlA)
//
// Sole call site: GameNet::HandlePkt07_AltGunDispatch 0x4341e0 — remote alt-gun
// fire replay needs the local controller matching the sender's weapon id.
//
// Source: D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\Player\\player_weapon.c (GameNet_ReplayRemoteGun support).
0x43c9c0 struct PlayerGunFireController* __fastcall Player::FindAltGunFireControllerForWeaponId(struct zUtil_SaveGameState* saveState, int32_t weaponId)
{
    struct PlayerState* playerState = saveState->playerState
    struct OptCatalogEntryDef* eax = OptCatalog::FindEntryById(weaponId)
    int32_t i = 2
    // lea edx, [esi+0x79C] — position loop cursor at altWeaponBanks[2].ctrlB.optCatalogEntry_00.
    // Derivation: 0x5EC (altWeaponBanks base) + 2*0xAC (skip banks 0,1) + 0x58 (ctrlB offset
    // within a bank) + 0x00 (optCatalogEntry_00 within ctrlB) = 0x79C.
    // The loop advances edx by 0xAC per iteration (bank stride) and reads both sides per
    // bank: ctrlB at [edx], ctrlA at [edx-0x54] (since ctrlA precedes ctrlB by 0x54 bytes).
    int32_t* edx = &playerState->altWeaponBanks[2].controllers[1]

    do
        if (edx[-0x15] == eax)
            return &playerState->altWeaponBanks[i].controllers

        if (*edx == eax)
            return &playerState->altWeaponBanks[i].controllers[1]

        i += 1
        edx = &edx[0x2b]
    while (i s< 0xa)

    return &playerState->altWeaponBanks[1].controllers

    // [comments not attached to rendered lines]
    // [comment @ 0x43c9d6]
    // Check ctrlA side first: `cmp [edx-0x54], eax` reads bank[i].ctrlA.optCatalogEntry_00
    // (ctrlA = ctrlB - 0x54). If it matches the resolved entry, jump to the ctrlA-return
    // block at 0x43c9f3 which computes &altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlA.
    // [comment @ 0x43c9db]
    // Check ctrlB side: `cmp [edx], eax` reads bank[i].ctrlB.optCatalogEntry_00 (edx still
    // points at the ctrlB slot). If it matches, jump to the ctrlB-return block at
    // 0x43ca09 which computes &altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlB. Priority note: ctrlA is checked
    // first so if both sides somehow share the same entry, ctrlA wins.
    // [comment @ 0x43c9eb]
    // Fallback: no bank in [2..9] owns this weapon id. Return &altWeaponBanks[1].ctrlA
    // (offset 0x69C from PlayerState). Bank 1 is the primary-variant lane used for
    // dispatches that aren't explicit alt-bank weapons — ensures caller always gets a
    // non-null controller even when weapon id resolution fails on this client.
    // [comment @ 0x43c9f3]
    // ctrlA-match return path. Computes &altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlA = esi + i*0xAC + 0x5F0
    // via i*43 = (i*7)*3 + i decomposition (shl-sub-lea-lea-lea pattern). The magic
    // 0x5F0 = altWeaponBanks base 0x5EC + ctrlA offset 0x4. i is still in ecx, not
    // the 2..9 decrementing counter — this is the first-match i.
    // [comment @ 0x43ca09]
    // ctrlB-match return path. Computes &altWeaponBanks[i].ctrlB = esi + i*0xAC + 0x644
    // via the same i*43 trick. Magic 0x644 = altWeaponBanks base 0x5EC + ctrlB offset 0x58.
}

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zWeapon\zwep_init.c
// Loads the optional KILL_VERB text for a weapon catalog entry, defaulting to the localized generic kill verb.
// BN limitation: the named node payload is a zReader_NodeType4_FirstString array, but a normal refresh reverts the local overlay and renders the string key as eax->value.u32 + 0xc instead of arr_04->firstString_0C.
0x43ca20 void __fastcall zWeapon_OptCatalog::LoadKillVerbString(struct zReader_Node* reader, struct OptCatalogEntryDef* entry)
{
    // Allocates the per-entry kill-verb text buffer (0x14 bytes).
    char* killVerbString = calloc(1, 0x14)
    entry->killVerbString = killVerbString
    struct zReader_Node* eax = zReader::GetNamedNode(reader, "KILL_VERB")

    if (eax == 0)
        strncpy(killVerbString, zLoc::GetMessageString(0x250), 0x13)
        return

    strncpy(killVerbString, zLoc::ResolveMessageKeyOrFallback(*(eax->value.u32 + 0xc)), 0x13)
}

// Mission/weapon-loadout availability helper. Called exclusively by Player::LoadWeaponBanksAndSelectDefaults (0x438d10) while loading a player's weapon banks. //
// Args (__fastcall; ecx is ignored and clobbered immediately):
// - edx: missionThreshold, the authored "unlock at or above mission N" value from the weapon spec; 0 stays locked in SP.
// - stack arg 0: packedWeaponSlotId, encoded as (bankDigit << 4) | sideDigit from weapon-spec name digits.
// - stack arg 1: availableOut, int32_t* receiving 0 locked or 1 available.
//

// - mission 11: 0x10, 0x11, 0x80 (MISSILE)
// - mission 12: 0x10, 0x11, 0x20

    networkWhitelistTable.missionSlotIds[3][2] = 0

    *availableOut = 0

    // [comment @ 0x43ca9a]
    // Start of on-stack whitelist-table init. The 0xD0-byte frame will hold a 4-dword
    // row per mission (stride 0x10), with packed slot ids (bank<<4)|side. The long
    // sequence of `mov dword [esp+N], <const>` that follows populates this table.
    // Zero-fill is done via esi=0 (from `xor esi, esi`) written to most slots;
    // populated slots get eax=0x11, edx=0x20, edi=0x31, or immediates like 0x10, 0x61,
    // 0x80 as per mission-row content. ecx is repurposed for both the 0x10 constant
    // (used in several slot writes) and later for a dead write of 0x4F0CC0.
    // [comment @ 0x43cadc]
    // mov ecx, 0x4F0CC0 — dead write. ecx is not read again before the next
    // function call (which passes args via stack or gets them from esi/edi). This
    // looks like leftover reserved-pointer setup from the original C source (likely
    // a global save-state or mission-tracker pointer) that the compiler kept after
    // dead-code elimination failed to remove it.
    // [comment @ 0x43cbe3]
    // Network-enabled path. Load packedWeaponSlotId from [esp+0xE0] into edx. Then
    // `shl edi, 4` converts missionId to the byte offset of the mission's row in
    // the on-stack whitelist table (16-byte row stride). ecx = edi selects the start
    // of the row; the loop below scans 4 dwords.
    // [comment @ 0x43cbf1]
    // Whitelist scan inner loop. `cmp edx, [esp+ecx-4]` reads the current slot from
    // the mission's row. The `-4` offset is not a bug — ecx was initialized to
    // missionId*0x10 and the table base sits at [esp+0x0C..]; the -4 correction
    // aligns the read with the table's actual start. First match jumps to the
    // "available=1" return at 0x43cc15; exhausted loop falls through to
    // "available=0" at 0x43cc00.
    // [comment @ 0x43cc2e]
    // Single-player path. Two tests in sequence:
    //   cmp ebx, esi  — ebx=missionThreshold, esi=0: is threshold 0? If yes → locked.
    //   cmp ebx, edi  — edi=currentMissionId (UNSHIFTED here — the shl happened only
    //                   on the net path). If threshold > missionId → not yet unlocked.
    // Both failures fall to 0x43cc4f ("write 0"). Only when threshold != 0 AND
    // threshold <= missionId does the SP path write 1 (block 8 at 0x43cc36).
    // [comment @ 0x43cc36]
    // SP "available" store: *availableOut = 1. Reached when the authored
    // missionThreshold is nonzero and <= current mission id. After this the function
    // tears down the 0xD0 frame and returns with retn 0x8 (2 stack args cleanup).
}

// ZAR save-game section writer for all deployed mines owned by the local player.
// Registered with zUtil_ZAR::RegisterSectionHandler at 0x4390a2 (inside
// Player::LoadWeaponBanksAndSelectDefaults) as the write-side callback for the
// Mines ZAR section; invoked by the ZAR framework whenever a save is serialized.
//
// Serialization format (one section, many blobs):
//  1. "DummyMineData" sentinel blob (0x60 bytes, data=1) — acts as a section-
//     header marker so the reader can locate the mine section even when no mines
//     are deployed. Written once unconditionally at the top.
//  2. Per-mine "MineData%03d" blobs (0x60 bytes each), indexed by ebx counter —
//     one blob per live mine runtime across all mine banks.
//
// Iteration domain (THE ONLY BANKS SEARCHED):
// - Outer: bank offset from 0x2B0 to <0x408, stride 0xAC → banks 4 and 5 only
// - Inner: side offset from 0x00 to <0xA8, stride 0x54 → ctrlA and ctrlB only
// The two-bank window corresponds exactly to:
// - bank 4 = P_HEMINE (ctrlA) / P_QMINE (ctrlB)   [Phoenix mines]
// - bank 5 = R_HEMINE (ctrlA) / R_QMINE (ctrlB)   [Raptor mines]
// Other alt banks (2, 3, 6..9) hold non-mine weapons and are not touched by this
// serializer — keeping save payloads proportional to actual deployed mines
// rather than enumerating all 9 banks.
//
// For each (bank, side) with a non-null optCatalogEntry_00:
//  - Copy the entry's name (first field, +0x00) into the on-stack blob buffer.
//  - Walk OptCatalog_MineIterator_Begin/_Next to visit every live runtime that
//    shares this entry.
//  - For each runtime, pack into the 0x60-byte blob:
//    * position (3 floats) from runtime +0x44..+0x4C
//    * scale (3 floats) from zClass_Object3D::gwObject3DGetScale(runtime+0xC)
//    * node name (up to 0x24 bytes) from zClass_Class::gwNodeGetName(runtime+0x4)
//  - Build the blob label via sprintf(buf, "MineData%03d", ebx++) and flush it
//    with zUtil_ZAR::WriteSectionBlob. ebx is the global (across all banks/sides)
//    mine counter, not per-bank.
//
// Error propagation:
// WriteSectionBlob returns nonzero on success. eax is threaded through both
// loops (tested at 0x43ccc1 outer and 0x43cccf inner) so a single failed blob
// write aborts the rest of the serialization and the function returns that zero
// through eax. The caller (ZAR framework) treats that as the section-write error
// signal.
//
// Runtime struct layout (inferred from this writer's reads):
// - +0x04 : node pointer (queried by gwNodeGetName for blob label payload)
// - +0x0C : 3D object pointer (queried by gwObject3DGetScale)
// - +0x44, +0x48, +0x4C : position x,y,z floats
//
// Globals:
// - g_GameStateOrMapTable at 0x4F3A88 — dereferenced as `->playerState` (+0x4)
//   to access the PlayerState; the mine iteration reads per-bank optCatalogEntry
//   pointers from altWeaponBanks starting at PlayerState + 0x5F0 (bank[0]+ctrlA).
// - strncpy IAT cached into ebp via `mov ebp, [0x4CC5A0]` at function entry and
//   called three times via `call ebp` to avoid repeated IAT dereferences. BN
//   renders these as the generic strncpy call, but watch out: if you renamed or
//   retyped strncpy, the three call sites inherit via ebp rather than via the
//   IAT directly.
//
// Magic constants:
// - 0x60 = per-mine blob payload size (matches the reader's blob size).
// - 0x24 = entry/node name buffer size (35 bytes + NUL via calloc zero; same as
//   KILL_VERB buffer size in zWeapon_OptCatalog::LoadKillVerbString).
// - 0x20 = second strncpy limit for the entry name.
// - 0x2B0 = PlayerState-relative start offset (bank 4 ctrlA minus the +0x5F0 base).
// - 0x408 = exclusive end offset (bank 6 ctrlA minus the +0x5F0 base; unreachable).
// - 0xAC = PlayerAltWeaponBankRuntime stride (bank step).
// - 0x54 = sizeof(PlayerGunFireController) (ctrlA→ctrlB step).
// - 0xA8 = 2*0x54 (inner loop upper bound = end of ctrlB).
// - "DummyMineData" string at 0x4DD234, "MineData%03d" fmt at 0x4DD224,
//   "Dummy" literal at 0x4DD244.
//
// Sole registration site: Player::LoadWeaponBanksAndSelectDefaults 0x4390a2 →
// zUtil_ZAR::RegisterSectionHandler at 0x4390b7.
//
// Source: D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\Player\\player_weapon.c (Mines save-section writer).
0x43cc70 int32_t __fastcall Player::WriteMinesZarSection(struct zZbdPreLoadCtx* ctx)

    // strncpy(&blob.name /*esp+0x60*/, "Dummy" /*0x4DD244*/, 0x24) — initialize the
    // section-header blob's name field to the string literal "Dummy". Only used for
    // the leading DummyMineData sentinel blob; subsequent per-mine blobs overwrite
    // this buffer with the real OptCatalog entry name before each write.

    // Write the "DummyMineData" section-header blob (0x60 bytes, data flag = 1).

    int32_t writeOk = zUtil_ZAR::WriteSectionBlob(ctx, "DummyMineData", &data, 0x60)

    // `[playerState + edx + innerCtrl + 0x5F0]` for optCatalogEntry lookups. With

    int32_t bankOffset = 0x2b0
    int32_t writeOkSaved = writeOk

        int32_t sideOffset = 0
        int32_t sideOffsetSaved = 0

    // Read optCatalogEntry for this (bank, side): edi = [playerState + edx + ecx + 0x5F0].
    // - edx is the bank offset (0x2B0 = bank4, 0x35C = bank5)
    // - ecx is the side offset (0 = ctrlA, 0x54 = ctrlB)
    // - 0x5F0 = altWeaponBanks base (0x5EC) + optCatalogEntry_00 position within ctrlA (0x04)

    // for single-loadout ships); skip forward to the next (bank, side) pair.

                    data.spawnPos.x = mineRuntime->posX
                    data.spawnPos.y = mineRuntime->posY
                    data.spawnPos.z = mineRuntime->posZ

    // name (typically auto-generated "Mine_<N>" or similar). The returned string is
    // strncpy'd (0x24 limit) into the blob's name field, overwriting the entry-name
    // copy done at 0x43ccf1. So the blob-name field semantics shift from
    // "entry-type label" to "actual runtime node name" for populated mines.
                    char* _Source = zClass_Class::gwNodeGetName(mineRuntime->ownerNode)
                    strncpy(&data.ownerNodeName, _Source, 0x24)
                    int32_t mineCount_1 = mineCount
                    mineCount += 1
    // sprintf(label, "MineData%03d", ebx++) — build the section-blob label using
    // the global mine counter (ebx). %03d pads to 3 digits with leading zeros, so
    // labels are MineData000, MineData001, ... ebx increments across ALL banks and
    // sides, giving a flat monotonic index irrespective of bank ordering.
                    char blobToken[0x14]
                    sprintf(&blobToken, "MineData%03d", mineCount_1)
                    writeOkSaved = zUtil_ZAR::WriteSectionBlob(ctx, &blobToken, &data, 0x60)

                bankOffset = bankOffsetSaved
                sideOffset = sideOffsetSaved
                writeOk = writeOkSaved

    // Inner loop step: advance side offset by 0x54 (ctrlA → ctrlB = 1 side). If
    // the new offset >= 0xA8 (= 2 * 0x54, i.e. past ctrlB), fall through to the
    // outer step at 0x43cdc0. Otherwise loop to 0x43cccf to process the next side
    // of the current bank.
            sideOffset += 0x54
            sideOffsetSaved = sideOffset

            if (sideOffset s>= 0xa8)
                break

    // Outer loop step: advance bank offset by 0xAC (bank stride). If the new offset
    // >= 0x408 (= 0x2B0 + 2*0xAC, i.e. past bank 5), exit to the epilogue at
    // 0x43cdd6. Otherwise loop to 0x43ccc1 to process the next bank (bank 5 after
    // bank 4). Only banks 4 and 5 are ever visited — other alt banks don't own
    // mines in this build.
        bankOffset += 0xac
        bankOffsetSaved = bankOffset

        if (bankOffset s>= 0x408)
            break

    return writeOk

    // [comments not attached to rendered lines]
    // [comment @ 0x43cc78]
    // Cache strncpy IAT pointer into ebp (`mov ebp, [0x4CC5A0]`). Used three times
    // below via `call ebp` instead of `call dword [strncpy]` — a compiler hot-loop
    // optimization to avoid the extra IAT fetch per call. All three sites are
    // strncpy(dst, src, len) cdecl pushes.
    // [comment @ 0x43ccd7]
    // Re-fetch the PlayerState fresh each outer iteration (via
    // g_GameStateOrMapTable at 0x4F3A88 → +0x4 playerState). Writing happens outside
    // this function's call-stack control, so the save-system could in theory swap
    // saveStates mid-iteration — the refetch keeps the pointer consistent with
    // current global state rather than snapshotted at function entry.
    // [comment @ 0x43ccf1]
    // Copy the entry's name string (entry->name at entry+0x00, via `mov edx, [edi]`)
    // into the blob's name field. strncpy with limit 0x20 — note this differs from
    // the earlier 0x24-sized buffer, so at most 0x20 bytes are filled with ≥4 bytes
    // of zero-padding guaranteed at the tail of the 0x24-byte slot.
    // [comment @ 0x43cd02]
    // OptCatalog_MineIterator_Begin(entry) — returns the first live runtime instance
    // owned by this entry (linked-list head), or null if no mines of this type are
    // deployed. The inner per-mine loop advances via OptCatalog_MineIterator_Next at
    // 0x43cd92 until null is returned.
    // [comment @ 0x43cd11]
    // Pack one mine runtime into the blob:
    //   [esp+0x20] data flag = 0 (distinguish from the sentinel blob's data=1)
    //   [esp+0x44..0x4C] = runtime position (runtime+0x44..+0x4C: x, y, z floats)
    //   [esp+0x58..0x60] = output of gwObject3DGetScale(runtime->obj3d /*+0xC*/)
    // lea ecx, [esi+0x44] is the base pointer to the position triplet; the three
    // `mov [esp+0xNN], reg` copies flatten them into the blob layout.
    // [comment @ 0x43cd87]
    // Write this mine's blob to the ZAR stream. Result stored in [esp+0x18] = eax,

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zFMV\fmv_script.cpp
//
// Synchronous play-to-completion driver for an FMV script.
//
// Sequence:
//   1. self->m_abortOnKey @ +0x10 := abortOnKey (kbd-press shortcut, consumed by Update).
//   2. zFMV_Script_BeginAtTime(self) — primes surface state, snapshots start time, fires the first action's Begin vfunc.
//   3. zFMV_Script_UpdateAtTime(self) once outside the loop; if it returns 0 immediately (no current action / Begin failed), skip into BeginNow rewind.

//   5. zFMV_Script_BeginNow(self, 0) — rewinds m_cur to m_head without freeing actions, leaving the script ready to replay.
//   6. Return 1 unconditionally.
//
// Calling convention: __thiscall, ECX = self, single stack arg `abortOnKey`, `retn 4` reclaims it. ESI is preserved across the loop as the cached self pointer (push/pop esi frame).

        do
            i = zFMV_Script::UpdateAtTime(self)
        while (i != 0)

    zFMV_Script::BeginNow(self, 0)

}

// Original file: GameZRecoil/zFMV/fmv_stream.cpp
// Per-tick driver of zFMV_Stream playback: optionally seeks, decodes one video frame, and pumps the double-buffered audio refill state machine. Returns the post-advance currentFrameIndex (or 0 on AVI / decoder error).
// 1. If frameIndex != 0xFFFFFFFF, override self->currentFrameIndex with frameIndex (caller-driven seek).
// 2. If currentFrameIndex >= aviVideoFrameCount: skip read+decode, fall through to step 4 (loop bookkeeping only).
// 3. Decode pipeline:
//    a. AVIStreamRead(stream, currentFrameIndex, 1, aviCompressedFrameBuffer, aviCompressedFrameBufferBytes, NULL, NULL)
//       → on failure log "Cannot Read AVI Video Stream" (zerr line 0x105) and return 0.
//    b. EnterCriticalSection(&self->audioLock).
//    c. ICDecompress(decompressor, 0, aviVideoFormatSrc, aviCompressedFrameBuffer, aviVideoFormatDst, imagePixels)
//       → on failure log "Cannot Decompress AVI Video Stream" (line 0x10c) and return 0 — BUG: returns while still holding audioLock (no LeaveCriticalSection on error path).
//    d. LeaveCriticalSection(&self->audioLock).
// 4. ++currentFrameIndex; wrap to 0 when it reaches aviVideoFrameCount (looping playback).
// 5. Audio pump (only when self->hasAudioTrack != 0):
//    a. If audioPlaybackStartPending != 0: zSndSample_PlayA3DSimple(audioSample) with gain=1.0f (literal 0x3f800000 pushed), clear pending, return currentFrameIndex (the rest of the audio block is skipped this tick — giving DirectSound one tick to actually start before refill begins).
//    b. Else if modeFlags != 0: classic ping-pong refill — keep the half NOT currently under the play cursor full of fresh PCM:
//       - audioRefillSecondHalfNext == 0 (we last filled second half / will fill SECOND next): when cursor entered second half (cursor > audioSegmentBytes), refill FIRST half via zFMV_Stream_FillAudioBuffer(self, offset=0, size=audioSegmentBytes) and set flag := 1.
//       - audioRefillSecondHalfNext != 0 (will fill FIRST next... NO, naming is "second-next"): when cursor returned to first half (0 < cursor < audioSegmentBytes), refill SECOND half via zFMV_Stream_FillAudioBuffer(self, offset=audioSegmentBytes, size=audioSegmentBytes) and clear flag := 0.

// Computes a Newell-method plane equation from a polygon's vertices. Same shape as zModel_Const::ComputePolygonPlaneEquation (Newell normal + centroid d-offset) but uses a fast Quake-style reciprocal-magnitude approximation (`fast_invsqrt(|n|^2)`) at 0x46c4ba (`(eax >> 1) + 0x1fc00000`) instead of a true `1.0 / sqrt`. //

// Reverses the tail of a zVec3 polygon point list in place, preserving points[0] as the anchor.
//
// Given `points[0..pointCount-1]`, the function produces `points[0], points[pointCount-1], points[pointCount-2], ..., points[1]` — i.e. it flips the winding order of a polygon without rotating the starting vertex.
//
// Algorithm (floor(pointCount/2) iterations):
//   front = &points[1];
//   back  = &points[pointCount - 1];
//   for (int i = 0; i < pointCount/2; ++i) {
//       zVec3 tmp = *back;
//       *back-- = *front;
//       *front++ = tmp;
//   }
//
// For pointCount in {0,1,2,3} the loop runs 0, 0, 1, 1 times respectively (pointCount=2 is a degenerate quad-swap that hits self-swap at the one iteration when back==front). For even pointCount the final iteration is back==front == middle+1 and performs a harmless self-copy.
//

//
// Source file: GameZRecoil/zGeometry/zgeo_convexify.cpp (confirmed via the `sub esp,0x10` prologue's file-origin tag — see first instruction's original-file comment on 0x46c5b0).
//

//   1. Attempted retype of edx_1/ecx_1 to zVec3* — SUCCESS (renders front/back as zVec3* with ->x/->y/->z).
//   2. Attempted set_function_prototype with zVec3* points — SUCCESS.
//   3. Acceptable — the eax_1/frontOld pair at 0x46c5bb is the MSVC `cdq; sub eax,edx; sar 1` rounding-toward-zero idiom.
//   4. `back = &points[pointCount] - 0xc` retains a raw -12 byte offset because BN cannot simultaneously apply zVec3* sizing to the base index AND a constant byte subtrahend. Documented by 0x46c5c3 address comment.
//   5. `frontStore` is still rendered as `float*` (not zVec3*) because the write stream uses three separate float stores (*frontStore, frontStore[1], frontStore[2]) — retyping to zVec3* would require BN to discover the aggregate store pattern; it currently keeps the element-granular view. // Ensures the first-triangle winding of a polygon (points[0..2]) produces a positive Z cross product — i.e. CCW winding when viewed from +Z. If not, either flip the polygon in place (allowReverse=1) or fail (allowReverse=0).

// Pump the keyboard DirectInput device queue and update g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable for one frame.
//
// Signature: void __fastcall(int8_t dispatchCallbacks). The boolean arrives in cl and is stashed in a local slot (esp+0x13 after the GetDeviceData call).
//
// Global state touched:
//   g_zInput_KbdDevice           @ 0x561cc8 -- IDirectInputDevice* (DirectInput 5/7 keyboard)
//   g_zInput_KbdEventBuffer      @ 0x561ccc -- DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA rgdod[128] working buffer
//   g_zInput_KbdModifierState    @ 0x561cd0 -- sticky modifier bitfield (ah: bit0=Alt, bit1=Ctrl, bit2=Shift)
//   g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable  @ 0x561cd4 -- struct zInput_KbdKeyDispatchEntry[0x7de] (2014 slots)
//   g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallback @ 0x565bc4 -- optional int32_t(__fastcall*)(int ascii, void* ctx)
//   g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallbackCtx @ 0x565bc8 -- ctx passed to the raw-event callback
//
// Dispatch table layout: each slot is indexed by (dikScanCode | (modifiers << 8)) giving the modifier-aware key-combo space used by the BindMap. Valid indices are [0..0x7de). Slot fields:
//   state      : small transition enum shared with Mouse/DI getters (0 idle, 1 held, 2 held-consumed, 4 down-edge)
//   callbackFn : int32_t (__fastcall *)(int32_t dikCodeWithMods) -- optional per-combo hot callback
//
// Flow:
//   1. Retrieve up to 128 DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA entries via g_zInput_KbdDevice->lpVtbl->GetDeviceData(this, cbObjectData=0x10, rgdod=&g_zInput_KbdEventBuffer[0], pdwInOut=&localCount{=0x80 in}, dwFlags=0) (vtable +0x28).
//      - On DIERR_INPUTLOST (0x8007001e) call Acquire() at vtable +0x1c and fall through with zero events.
//      - On any other error, route to zInput_DI_ErrorToString with error code 0x170 and the format buffer at 0x4e08cc, then return.
//
//   2. Process-loop (edi = event index 0..localCount):
//      For each DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA at esi (stride 0x10):
//        a. Branch on dwOfs via a jump table at 0x46f8ac keyed by (dwOfs - 0x1d); out-of-range goes to the generic path.
//        b. Modifier path (Alt/Ctrl/Shift keys): test dwData bit 7 (key-pressed flag), update bit 0/1/2 of g_zInput_KbdModifierState's ah byte accordingly, then jump to the shared tail.
//        c. Generic key path: if g_zInput_KbdModifierState is non-zero AND the existing slot state is non-zero, force slot state = 4 (down-edge pending) so a held modifier + new keystroke produces a fresh edge. Then copy the current modifier bits into the post-processed flag byte at dwData:
//            modBit Alt   (ah&1) -> dwData |= 0x40
//            modBit Ctrl  (ah&2) -> dwData |= 0x20
//            modBit Shift (ah&4) -> dwData |= 0x10
//          and OR the modifier bits (<<8) into the slot index for the state write-back.
//        d. Shared tail (0x46f7c2): look up the slot and update its state.
//           If dwData bit 7 (key pressed): state = (prev == 1 ? 3 : 1) via the dec/neg/sbb/and 0xfe/add 3 idiom -- held-first-frame or held-consumed.
//           Otherwise (key released): set state bit 2 (|=4), marking a down->up edge. If g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallback is non-null, call zInput_KBD_TranslateDikToAscii(dikCode) to get the ASCII value and invoke the raw callback with (ascii, g_zInput_KbdRawEventCallbackCtx).
//
//   3. If dispatchCallbacks is non-zero, second loop (ebp = event index) walks the same DIDEVICEOBJECTDATA buffer to invoke per-combo hot callbacks:
//      a. Rebuild the combined (dikCode | modifierBits<<8) index from the flag bits written in step 2c.
//      b. Bounds-check esi against 0x7de.
//      c. If slot.callbackFn != NULL AND slot.state has bit 0 set (keyHeld signal), invoke callbackFn(ecx=combo) and clear the slot state to 0 ("consume the edge").
//
// BN rendering note: the `*(dwOfs + 0x46f8ab)` lookup is really assembly `eax = dwOfs - 0x1d; dl = byte [eax+0x46f8c8]`, indexing the embedded byte lookup table after the function's return/jump-table region. The state update remains the VC6 dec/neg/sbb/and/add branchless idiom.
//
// Return via `add esp, 8; ret` (cdecl-style callee stack cleanup of the 8-byte local, but no stack args).
//
// Call sites: per-frame input pump from the main loop; also called from zInput_KBD_WaitForAnyKeyPress which sets dispatchCallbacks=0 so a blocking wait does not fire registered callbacks.

// Consume-on-read transition-state query for a packed DIK key combo index in g_zInputKbdKeyDispatchTable. If state has bit 2 set, returns the original state and clears it to 0; if state is exactly 1, promotes the stored state to 2 while returning 1.

{

}

// Format a packed key code into a human-readable combo string like 'Ctrl-A'.
//
// packedKey layout (low 11 bits of a packed binding slot):
//   bits [0..7]  = DIK scan code, indexing g_zInput_DikKeyNames[2014] at 0x565ebc (each slot is a char*).
//   bit 8        = Alt     -> prefix string at 0x4e0914 ('Alt-')
//   bit 9        = Ctrl    -> prefix string at 0x4e091c ('Ctrl-')
//   bit 10       = Shift   -> prefix string at 0x4e090c ('Shift-')
//
// If the DIK slot is empty (name table pointer is NULL for that scan code), writes nothing and returns the global empty-name placeholder k_EmptyString at 0x4e5ce0.
//
// Otherwise zeroes destBuf[0], then calls strncat at [0x4cc4f0] (prototype (dest, src, maxlen)) in sequence Ctrl-, Alt-, Shift-, KeyName. After each concat, strlen's dest and decrements the remaining byte budget carried in esi. Returns destBuf.
//
// Modifier test order in assembly:
//   test ah, 0x2 -> bit 9 Ctrl  -> push 0x4e091c 'Ctrl-'
//   test ah, 0x1 -> bit 8 Alt   -> push 0x4e0914 'Alt-'
//   test ah, 0x4 -> bit 10 Shift -> push 0x4e090c 'Shift-'
//
// ret 0xc = 3 stack args (stdcall). The 'push ecx' at entry is only a local scratch slot later caching the DIK name table entry pointer for the final strncat call; it is not a this-pointer, and this function is not a method of BindMapContext.
//
// BN limitation: the local scratch slot still appears as keyNameSlot/keyNameSlotScratch at the top of HLIL, and inline strlen scans after strncat render as repne-scasb loops instead of strlen(destBuf).
//
// Likely source: zinput.cpp
0x470f80 char* __stdcall zInput::BindMap_FormatKeyComboName(int32_t packedKey, char* destBuf, int32_t maxBytes)
{

    char** keyNameSlotScratch = keyNameSlot
    int16_t eax = packedKey.w
    uint32_t ecx_1 = eax.b

    if (g_zInput_DikKeyNames[ecx_1] == 0)
        return &k_EmptyString

    int32_t _Count = maxBytes
    *destBuf = 0

    if ((eax:1.b & 2) != 0)
        char* edi_1 = strncat(destBuf, "Ctrl-", _Count)
        int32_t i = 0xffffffff

        while (i != 0)
            bool cond:2_1 = 0 != *edi_1
            edi_1 = &edi_1[1]
            i -= 1

            if (not(cond:2_1))
                break

        eax = packedKey.w
        _Count -= not.d(i) - 1

    if ((eax:1.b & 1) != 0)
        char* edi_2 = strncat(destBuf, "Alt-", _Count)
        int32_t i_1 = 0xffffffff

        while (i_1 != 0)
            bool cond:3_1 = 0 != *edi_2
            edi_2 = &edi_2[1]
            i_1 -= 1

            if (not(cond:3_1))
                break

        eax = packedKey.w
        _Count -= not.d(i_1) - 1

    if ((eax:1.b & 4) != 0)
        char* edi_3 = strncat(destBuf, "Shift-", _Count)
        int32_t i_2 = 0xffffffff

        while (i_2 != 0)
            bool cond:4_1 = 0 != *edi_3
            edi_3 = &edi_3[1]
            i_2 -= 1

            if (not(cond:4_1))
                break

        _Count -= not.d(i_2) - 1

    return strncat(destBuf, g_zInput_DikKeyNames[ecx_1], _Count)

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zMath\zMath_Quat.cpp -- void zMath_Quat_Multiply(const zQuat* a, const zQuat* b, zQuat* outAB).
// Hamilton product of two unit quaternions, out = a * b:
//   w = a.w*b.w - a.x*b.x - a.y*b.y - a.z*b.z
//   x = a.w*b.x + a.x*b.w + a.y*b.z - a.z*b.y
//   y = a.w*b.y + a.y*b.w + a.z*b.x - a.x*b.z
//   z = a.w*b.z + a.z*b.w + a.x*b.y - a.y*b.x
// __fastcall: ecx=a, edx=b, stack arg=outAB. Used by zEffect::AnimateNodeOverTime to compose incremental frame rotations.
0x475910 void __fastcall zMath::QuatMultiply(struct zQuat const* quatA, struct zQuat const* quatB, struct zQuat* outAB)
{
    outAB->w = quatB->w * quatA->w - quatA->x * quatB->x - quatA->y * quatB->y - quatA->z * quatB->z
    outAB->x = quatB->w * quatA->x + quatA->w * quatB->x + quatB->z * quatA->y - quatA->z * quatB->y
    outAB->y = quatB->w * quatA->y + quatA->w * quatB->y + quatA->z * quatB->x - quatB->z * quatA->x
    outAB->z = quatB->w * quatA->z + quatA->w * quatB->z + quatB->y * quatA->x - quatA->y * quatB->x
}

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zMath\zMath_Quat.cpp
// Computes outAConjB = quatA * conjugate(quatB), which is the inverse multiply used for unit quaternions. ECX=quatA, EDX=quatB, stack arg=outAConjB, and the function callee-cleans the one stack pointer argument.
0x4759d0 void __fastcall zMath::QuatMultiplyInverse(struct zQuat* quatA, struct zQuat* quatB, struct zQuat* outAConjB)
{

    outAConjB->x = quatB->w * quatA->x - quatA->w * quatB->x - quatB->z * quatA->y + quatA->z * quatB->y
    outAConjB->y = quatB->w * quatA->y - quatA->w * quatB->y - quatA->z * quatB->x + quatB->z * quatA->x
    outAConjB->z = quatB->w * quatA->z - quatA->w * quatB->z - quatB->y * quatA->x + quatA->y * quatB->x
}

//

//
// Returns 0 when reusable, non-zero (1 or +/-1 from sbb idiom) otherwise.
//
// Algorithm:
// 1. Quick-reject: if lhs->currentTextureDirectoryEntry != rhs->currentTextureDirectoryEntry, return 1.
// 2. Compare the first 32 bytes byte-for-byte via `rep cmpsb` — that covers flags, packedColor, colorRgb, currentTextureDirectoryEntry, unknown_14, unknown_18, unknown_1c (offsets 0..0x1f).     bool z = currentTextureDirectoryEntry == currentTextureDirectoryEntry

    while (i != 0)
        char temp2_1 = lhs_1->flags.b
        char temp3_1 = rhs_1->flags.b
        c = temp2_1 u< temp3_1
        z = temp2_1 == temp3_1
        lhs_1 = &lhs_1->flags + 1
        rhs_1 = &rhs_1->flags + 1
        i -= 1

        if (not(z))
            break

    if (not(z))
        bool c_1 = unimplemented  {sbb eax, eax}
        result = sbb.d(sbb.d(0, 0, c), 0xffffffff, c_1)

// Original file: Battlesport/zModel/gmod_const.c
//
// struct zDi* __cdecl zModel_DiPool_AllocFromFreeList(void)
//
// Pop the head of the zDi free list and return a zeroed, flagged zDi slot.
//
//   1. slotIndex = g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex.  If negative (empty), report
//      "Creating Model3D; model buffer full" via zError::ReportOld and return 0.
//   2. entry = &g_zModel_DiPoolBase[slotIndex]  (sizeof(zDi) == 88 == 0x58).
//   3. Pop: g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex = entry->nextFreeIndex.
//   4. g_zModel_DiPoolInUseCount++.
//   5. memset(entry, 0, 0x54) — clear all 84 payload bytes; leave nextFreeIndex
//      intact (the FreeIfUnreferenced/relink code expects it).
//   6. entry->flags = (entry->flags & 0xDF) | 3 — flags bit0|bit1 set, bit5 clear.
//      (After the memset, flags is already 0, so this just writes 3.)
//   7. Return entry.
//
// Paired with zModel_DiPool::FreeIfUnreferenced @ 0x4820f0 which pushes back onto the free list.
//
// Note on variables:
//   - slotByteOffsetDiv8 = slotIndex * 11; the byte offset into the pool is
//     slotByteOffsetDiv8 * 8 = slotIndex * 88.  MSVC factored the multiply to
//     keep the *8 inside an x86 LEA scale factor.
//   - diPoolBase typed zModel_DiSlotLinkView* (identical 88-byte layout, but
//     exposes diPayloadWords[21] + nextFreeIndex for the free-list traversal).
0x482080 struct zDi* zModel_DiPool::AllocFromFreeList()
{

        zError::ReportOldNoOp(0x400, "D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zModel\gmod_const.c", 0x4a1, "ERROR: Creating Model3D; model buffer full.")
        return 0

    // slot byte offset factored as (slotIndex*11)*8 so MSVC can use LEA scale-8. entry = &g_zModel_DiPoolBase[slotIndex]; sizeof(zDi) == 88 == 0x58 == 11*8.
    int32_t slotByteOffsetDiv8 = slotIndex * 0xb
    struct zModel_DiSlotLinkView* diPoolBase = g_zModel_DiPoolBase
    struct zDi* entry = &diPoolBase->diPayloadWords[slotByteOffsetDiv8 * 2]
    int32_t diPoolInUseCount = g_zModel_DiPoolInUseCount
    g_zModel_DiPoolFreeHeadIndex = (&diPoolBase->nextFreeIndex)[slotByteOffsetDiv8 * 2]
    g_zModel_DiPoolInUseCount = diPoolInUseCount + 1
    // rep stosd of 0x15 dwords = memset(entry, 0, 0x54). Zeroes all zDi fields through bboxRadius (0..83); preserves nextFreeIndex at offset 84 (the free-list link).
    __builtin_memset(entry, 0, 0x54)
    // entry->flags = (0 & 0xdf) | 3 = 3 after preceding memset. Sets flag bits 0+1 (INITIALIZED | IN_USE), clears bit 5.
    int32_t eax_2
    eax_2.b = entry->flags.b & 0xdf
    eax_2.b |= 3
    entry->flags = eax_2
    return entry

    // [comment @ 0x4820b4]
    // Read nextFreeIndex (offset +0x54 = 84) of slot to pop the head of the free list.
}

// Returns true for null-safe DI flags 0x04/0x08/0x20, or when any zDiEntry material has auxiliary material data.

    // [comment @ 0x483a9e]

// zDi_SetCurrentVariantCycleTextureCount — set the cycle-texture frame count
// on the current zDiEntry's material slot.
//
// Forwarder/validator that walks zDi → zDiEntry → zModel_Material and forwards
// the texture count to zModel_Material_SetCycleTextureCount. NULL-zDi guard with
// debug-print error path; NULL-materialRef "fallback" is buggy (see below) but
// unreachable for any zDi loaded by the world loader.
//
// Prototype: int32_t __fastcall(struct zDi* di, int32_t textureCount)

//

//   -1 (0xffffffff) if di == NULL (caller error; logged to stderr)
//
// Walk:
//
//   Phase 1 (0x484250..0x484252) — di NULL guard.
//     test ecx, ecx; jne block 2.
//
//   Phase 2-error (0x484254..0x48428b) — di == NULL fast path.
//     Format error message into g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer @ 0x575de0:

//        "D:\\Proj\\GameZRecoil\\zModel\\gmod_const.c", line 0xf3f (3903)
//     Then fprintf(stderr, &g_zError_DebugMsgBuffer).
//     stderr is loaded as `[g__iob @ 0x4cc4f8] + 0x40` — the third FILE slot in
//     the CRT _iob array.
//     Returns -1 via `or eax, 0xffffffff`.
//
//   Phase 2-walk (0x48428c..0x484294) — Walk to materialRef.
//     ecx = di->entries           [+0x30, struct zDiEntry*]
//     ecx = entries->materialRef  [+0x14, struct zModel_Material*]
//     test/jne block 4.
//
//   Phase 3-call (0x48429e..0x4842a5) — Normal path: forward to material setter.
//     EDX still holds caller's textureCount.
//     call zModel_Material_SetCycleTextureCount(matRef=ECX, textureCount=EDX)
//     return 0.
//
//   Phase 3-bug (0x484296..0x48429d) — UNREACHABLE in practice (BUG path).
//     Reached when di->entries->materialRef == NULL. ECX is NULL at this point.
//     The instruction `and word [ecx], 0xfbff` would dereference NULL and crash
//     if ever taken. Almost certainly an original-source bug:
//       - The intent was probably "clear the cycle-texture flag on this entry/DI
//         so the renderer doesn't try to advance it." The author likely meant
//         `*(matRef-pointer-to-something-else)` but forgot to reload the pointer.
//       - In all observed game-data paths, materialRef is populated by the world
//         loader before any caller of this function sees the DI, so the path is
//         not exercised. The function's behavior on this edge would be a crash,
//         not a silent return.
//     Returns 0 if it ever did fall through (xor eax, eax; retn).
//

//

//
//   zInterp_Context_DispatchCoreCommand @ 0x4c295a

//
// Globals & data:

//   g__iob                  @ 0x4cc4f8 — pointer to CRT _iob[0]; +0x40 = stderr

//   &fprintf                @ 0x4cc5bc — CRT import slot

//
// Source attribution:

//

// Source file: GameZRecoil/zUtil/zutl_zar.cpp
//
// Appends a payload to the tail of a circular doubly-linked zArchiveList (payload list — the nodes hold `payload` plus `prev`/`next` pointers).
//
// Semantics:
//   - If list is NULL, return -1 (0xFFFFFFFF) — no allocation performed.
//   - Allocate a new zUtilFileIndexNode wrapping `payload` via zUtil_ZRDR_AllocNodeWithPayload.
//   - Empty-list path (list->head == NULL): set list->head = newNode and self-link it (newNode->prev = newNode->next = newNode), establishing a singleton circular list.
//   - Non-empty-list path: splice newNode between head->prev (the existing tail) and head via zArchiveList_LinkNodeBetween(tail, newNode, head). This preserves circular invariants.
//   - Increment list->count. Return the new count.
//
// Returns: int32_t — new count after insertion, or -1 on NULL-list failure.
//
// Layout reminder (zArchiveList): { int32_t count @ 0x0; int32_t[3] reserved @ 0x4; zUtilFileIndexNode* head @ 0x10 }.
0x48ca30 int32_t __fastcall zArchiveList::PushBackPayload(struct zArchiveList* list, void* payload)
{
    if (list == 0)
        return 0xffffffff

    struct zUtilFileIndexNode* newNode = zUtil_ZRDR::AllocNodeWithPayload(payload)
    struct zUtilFileIndexNode* head = list->head

    if (head != 0)
        zArchiveList::LinkNodeBetween(head->prev, newNode, head)
        int32_t newCountLinked = list->count + 1
        list->count = newCountLinked
        return newCountLinked

    list->head = newNode
    newNode->next = newNode
    newNode->prev = newNode
    int32_t newCountEmpty = list->count + 1
    list->count = newCountEmpty
    return newCountEmpty
}

// Original file: GameZRecoil/zUtil/zutl_zar.cpp
0x48ca70 int32_t __fastcall zArchiveList::RemovePayload(struct zArchiveList* list, void* payload)
{

        return 0xffffffff

    if (list->count == 0)
        return 0xffffffff

    if (node == 0)
        return 0xffffffff

    if (list->count == 1)
        zArchiveList::FreeNode(node)

        list->count = count - 1

    node->next->prev = node->prev

    list->count = result
    return result
}

// zArchiveList_FindPayloadByValue(zArchiveList* list, uint32_t value)
//   Locate the first payload in the list whose leading dword equals
//   `value`, and return that payload pointer (NOT the node). Returns
//   NULL when the list is empty or no match exists.
//
// ABI: __fastcall (ECX=list, EDX=value), no stack args.
//
// Algorithm:
//   1. Reject NULL list and empty list (list->count == 0).
//   2. Walk the circular doubly-linked node ring starting at list->head.
//   3. At each step, dereference node->payload and compare *(uint32_t*)
//      payload against `value`. Match -> return node->payload.
//   4. Loop terminates when the cursor wraps back to head.
//
// Layout reminders (already typed):
//   zArchiveList: count@0x00, head@0x10
//   zUtilFileIndexNode: payload@0x00, next@0x04, prev@0x08
//
// Sole caller: zEffect::AcquireRuntimeEntryByIndex @ 0x4620e5, which
// stores zEffect runtime entries with their per-entry index at the
// start of the payload struct, so this is effectively
// "find_runtime_entry_by_index" in that context. Helper lives in the
// generic zArchiveList runtime (GameZRecoil/zUtil/zutl_zar.cpp).
0x48cc20 void* __fastcall zArchiveList::FindPayloadByValue(struct zArchiveList* list, uint32_t value)
{
    if (list != 0 && list->count != 0)
        struct zUtilFileIndexNode* head = list->head
        struct zUtilFileIndexNode* next = head

        if (*next->payload == value)
            return next->payload

        while (true)
            next = next->next

            if (next == head)
                return 0

            if (*next->payload == value)
                return next->payload

    return 0
}

0x4a3e50 void __thiscall zSndFadeList::DeleteNodeAndAdvanceCursor(struct zSndFadeListHead* listHead, struct zSndFadeListNode** outCursor, struct zSndFadeListNode* node)

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Destructor of zIndexArchive (the struct itself is owned by the caller — e.g. a stack-local in zSndSampleSet_Init or a slot inside the mount table in zArchive_MountIndexArchive):
//
//   1. zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(self)   — flushes on dirty, closes hFile, frees records[] and resets all fields.
//   2. if (self->reservedFree != nullptr) free(self->reservedFree) — frees the auxiliary buffer that the mount/load path stashed at offset 0 (e.g. the slurped index image).
//
// reservedFree is not cleared after free(); that's fine because CloseAndFreeRecords already zeroed it via FreeRecordsAndReset before this second free runs — confirm by reading order: CloseAndFreeRecords sets reservedFree=0 in FreeRecordsAndReset's epilogue, so the subsequent test on the local copy (captured BEFORE the call into CloseAndFreeRecords via the esi live-register reuse) is the archived original value of reservedFree. //
// Actually the assembly is:
//   mov esi, ecx              ; esi = self
//   call CloseAndFreeRecords  ; ecx = self -- corrupts esi? No, esi is callee-saved.
//   mov esi, [esi]            ; esi = self->reservedFree  -- AFTER the call, so AFTER FreeRecordsAndReset zeroed it
//
// So the test always sees 0 here and the free is unreachable at runtime when the archive was ever opened. The branch exists for the uninitialized-slot path, where FreeRecordsAndReset's early-return (records==0) skips the field-zeroing and reservedFree is whatever the caller left it.

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Grow self->records[] to hold at least requiredCount zZarFileRecord entries.
//
// Algorithm (standard grow-by-2 dynamic array):
//   if (requiredCount < recordCapacity) return;        // already big enough (note: strict <, so capacity == requiredCount still grows)
//   newCapacity = max(recordCapacity * 2, requiredCount + 1);
//   self->recordCapacity = newCapacity;
//   self->records = realloc(self->records, newCapacity * sizeof(zZarFileRecord));  // sizeof=0x94
//
// Notes:
//   - Initial call with recordCapacity=0 picks branch requiredCount+1 (since 2*0==0 <= requiredCount+1).
//   - realloc(NULL, size) is equivalent to malloc(size), which is the path hit on the first call from zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail.
//   - Return value of realloc is stored unchecked — OOM would null self->records and subsequent access would crash; the engine treats allocation failure as fatal.
//   - Byte-count formula: edx = eax + 4*(9*eax) = 37*eax, then <<2 = 148*eax = 0x94*eax.
//   - recordCount is unchanged; only capacity grows.
//   - Callers: zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail, zIndexArchive::AddFileRecord.
0x4a62f0 void __thiscall zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(struct zIndexArchive* self, int32_t requiredCount)
{
    int32_t recordCapacity = self->recordCapacity

    if (requiredCount u< recordCapacity)
        return

    int32_t newCapacity = recordCapacity * 2

    if (newCapacity u<= requiredCount + 1)
        newCapacity = requiredCount + 1

    self->recordCapacity = newCapacity
    self->records = realloc(self->records, newCapacity * 0x94)
}

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Append the in-memory zZarFileRecord table to EOF of self->hFile and write the 8-byte trailer, so the archive file layout becomes:
//   [<file data>...][records[recordCount] (recordCount*0x94 bytes)][uint32 magic=1][uint32 recordCount]
//
// Step by step:
//   SetFilePointer(hFile, 0, NULL, FILE_END)           -- seek to end
//   WriteFile(hFile, self->records, recordCount*0x94, &bytesWritten, NULL)  -- records (sizeof(zZarFileRecord)=0x94)
//   WriteFile(hFile, &magic=1,         4, &bytesWritten, NULL)               -- trailer magic
//   WriteFile(hFile, &self->recordCount, 4, &bytesWritten, NULL)             -- trailer recordCount
//   self->dirty = 0
//
// Byte-count formula in assembly: edi = recordCount + 4*(9*recordCount) = 37*recordCount, then <<2 = 148*recordCount = 0x94*recordCount (= recordCount * sizeof(zZarFileRecord)).
//
// Note: return values from SetFilePointer/WriteFile are ignored; no error checking.
0x4a6360 void __fastcall zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    int32_t recordCount = self->recordCount
    HANDLE hFile = self->hFile
    uint32_t numberOfBytesWritten = 0
    int32_t buffer = 1
    // Append the in-memory record table to EOF, then write the 8-byte footer {magic=1, recordCount} and clear self->dirty.
    SetFilePointer(hFile, 0, nullptr, FILE_END)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, self->records, recordCount * 0x94, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, &buffer, 4, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    WriteFile(self->hFile, &self->recordCount, 4, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    self->dirty = 0
}

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp.
//
// Parse the trailer of the already-open self->hFile and load the zZarFileRecord index table into memory.
//
// On-disk layout (written by zIndexArchive::FlushIndexToTail):
//   [<raw file data>...]
//   [records[recordCount]  (recordCount * sizeof(zZarFileRecord) = recordCount * 0x94 bytes)]
//   [uint32_t magic=1]        // 4 bytes
//   [uint32_t recordCount]    // 4 bytes
//   <-- EOF
//
// Algorithm:
//   1. size = GetFileSize(hFile); if (size < 8) return 0;              // too small to hold trailer
//   2. Seek EOF-8 (FILE_END, -8).
//   3. Read 4 bytes -> footerMagic
//   4. Read 4 bytes -> recordCountFromTail
//   5. if (footerMagic != 1) return 0;                                 // not a valid zIndexArchive
//   6. zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(self, recordCountFromTail)        // grow records[] to fit
//   7. Seek EOF-(8 + recordCountFromTail*0x94) (FILE_END).
//   8. Read recordCountFromTail*0x94 bytes into self->records.
//   9. Seek 0 (FILE_BEGIN)                                             // restore for subsequent zReader reads
//  10. self->recordCount = recordCountFromTail
//  11. return 1
//
// Return values of ReadFile/SetFilePointer are not checked — if a partial read happens the records array is trusted to have been filled.
//
// Byte-count formula: edi = eax + 4*(9*eax) = 37*eax, then <<2 = 148*eax = 0x94*eax, matching FlushIndexToTail.
0x4a63f0 int32_t __thiscall zIndexArchive::LoadIndexFromTail(struct zIndexArchive* self)
{
    if (GetFileSize(self->hFile, nullptr) u< 8)
        return 0

    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0xfffffff8, nullptr, FILE_END)
    uint32_t numberOfBytesRead
    int32_t footerMagic
    ReadFile(self->hFile, &footerMagic, 4, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)
    int32_t recordCountFromTail
    ReadFile(self->hFile, &recordCountFromTail, 4, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)

    if (footerMagic != 1)
        return 0

    // Tail-load path: validate the 8-byte footer, ensure record capacity, read recordCount*0x94 bytes of zZarFileRecord data from EOF-(8+tableSize), then seek back to the file start.
    zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(self, recordCountFromTail)
    int32_t nNumberOfBytesToRead = recordCountFromTail * 0x94
    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0xfffffff8 - nNumberOfBytesToRead, nullptr, FILE_END)
    ReadFile(self->hFile, self->records, nNumberOfBytesToRead, &numberOfBytesRead, nullptr)
    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0, nullptr, FILE_BEGIN)
    self->recordCount = recordCountFromTail
    return 1
}

// Original file: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zUtil\zutl_zar.cpp. Appends data at EOF, builds a zZarFileRecord for the payload, copies it into records[recordCount], increments recordCount, marks the archive dirty, and returns whether WriteFile wrote dataSize bytes.
0x4a64d0 bool __thiscall zIndexArchive::AddFileRecord(struct zIndexArchive* self, char const* name, void const* data, uint32_t dataSize, char const* sourceTempPathOrNull, struct _FILETIME const* sourceFileTimeOrNull)
{
    int32_t recordCount = self->recordCount
    zIndexArchive::EnsureCapacity(self, recordCount + 1)
    SetFilePointer(self->hFile, 0, nullptr, FILE_END)
    // Build a transient zZarFileRecord for the new payload, optionally mark/store the source temp path + FILETIME, append the data bytes at EOF, copy the record into self->records[recordCount], then bump recordCount and mark the archive dirty.
    struct zZarFileRecord record
    record.fileOffset = GetFileSize(self->hFile, nullptr)
    record.fileSize = dataSize

    if (sourceTempPathOrNull != 0)
        record.recordFlags |= 2
        strncpy(&record.sourceTempPath, sourceTempPathOrNull, 0x40)
        record.sourceFileTime.dwLowDateTime = sourceFileTimeOrNull->dwLowDateTime
        record.sourceFileTime.dwHighDateTime = sourceFileTimeOrNull->dwHighDateTime

    strncpy(&record.name, name, 0x40)
    uint32_t numberOfBytesWritten
    WriteFile(self->hFile, data, dataSize, &numberOfBytesWritten, nullptr)
    __builtin_memcpy(&self->records[recordCount], &record, 0x94)
    bool result = numberOfBytesWritten == dataSize
    self->recordCount += 1
    self->dirty = 1
    return result
}
