// Runs the FxPass3 postprocess pipeline against the engine's primary surface and queues a primitive for it.
//
// Lock gate (run only if either condition is met):
//   g_zVideo_RendererType (@ 0x632120) != ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_SOFTWARE  -- hardware backend always locks
//   || g_zVideo_UseHalfResBackbuffer (@ 0x632128) != 0                    -- software half-res mode also locks
// If gated in, call g_zVideo_pfnLockSurfaceState(&g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState @ 0x632220) to lock the primary buffer for CPU access.
//
// Pipeline (always runs regardless of the lock gate -- operates on whatever surface state is currently published in g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState):
//   zRndr_SetFrameBufferRegion(pixels, NULL, 0, pitch)                   -- bind framebuffer for raster ops
//   zVideo_fx_SetSurfaceState(pixels, width, height, pitch)               -- update FX surface descriptor (writes 4 globals + derives pitch-in-pixels)
//   zVideo_FxPass3_QueuePrimitive(pixels, width, height, pitch)           -- enqueue the postprocess primitive into g_zVideo_FxPass3ConfigLocal
//
// Surface state field offsets (struct zVideo_SurfaceState, base 0x632220):
//   +0 width  +4 height  +8 pitch  +0xc lockInfoValid  +0x10 pixels  +0x14 locked  +0x18 pageLockActive  +0x1c surf
//
// Unlock gate (different from lock gate -- only software half-res unlocks here, hardware backends defer unlock to the dispatch layer):
//   if g_zVideo_UseHalfResBackbuffer != 0: g_zVideo_pfnUnlockSurfaceState(&g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState)
//
// Returns void (xor eax,eax). Calling convention: __cdecl, no args, balanced stack. Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\zVideo.cpp.
0x4a6840 void zVideo::RunPostprocessOnPrimaryBuffer()
{
    if (g_zVideo_RendererType != ZVID_RENDERER_BACKEND_SOFTWARE || g_zVideo_UseHalfResBackbuffer != 0)
        g_zVideo_pfnLockSurfaceState(&g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState)

    zRndr::SetFrameBufferRegion(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, nullptr, 0, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)
    zVideo::Fx_SetSurfaceState(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.width, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.height, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)
    // BN still misrenders the wrapper call order here. Assembly passes (pitchBytes=g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch, primitive=g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, width=g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.width, height=g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.height) into zVideo_FxPass3_QueuePrimitive.
    zVideo::FxPass3_QueuePrimitive(g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pixels, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.width, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.height, g_zVideo_PrimarySurfaceState.pitch)

//
//   if (zVideo_dd_PrepareWindowForMode() != 0)         // Win32: WS_POPUP | WS_EX_TOPMOST style + palette snapshot. Always returns 0, so this branch is effectively dead in current build.

//   return rc != 0 ? 1 : 0;                            // standard `neg eax; sbb eax,eax; neg eax` bool-normalize idiom
//
// Returns 0 = success, 1 = failure. Direct in-binary callees: zVideo_dd_PrepareWindowForMode (✅), zVideo_dd_CreateDirectDraw2ForSelectedDevice (✅). // Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zVideo\zvid_ddd3d.c -- returns the largest power of two <= value.
0x4ad680 int32_t __fastcall zVideo_dd3d::FloorPowerOfTwo(int32_t value) __pure
{
    int32_t eax = 1

    do
        eax <<= 1
    while (eax s< value)

    if (eax != value)
        return eax s>> 1

    return value
}

// Source: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zWeapon\zWeapon.cpp
// Blends each axis of a direction vector toward a target direction using per-axis weights, then normalizes the result.
0x4ae380 void __fastcall OptCatalog::BlendDirectionTowardTarget(struct zVec3* direction, struct zVec3* targetDirection, float xWeight, float yWeight, float zWeight)
{
    direction->x = (targetDirection->x - direction->x) * xWeight + direction->x
    direction->y = (targetDirection->y - direction->y) * yWeight + direction->y
    direction->z = (targetDirection->z - direction->z) * zWeight + direction->z
    zMath::Vec3Normalize(direction)
}

// Flushes the staged zOptionEntry list back to the Windows registry.
//
// LIKELY SOURCE: D:\Proj\GameZRecoil\zGame\zgame_opt.c
//
// --- PATH COMPOSITION (alloca'd stack buffer, rounded up to DWORD) ---
// Builds `SOFTWARE\<RegKeyRoot>\<RegKeyCurrentUser>\<RegKeyGame>` via five
// inline strlen+memcpy+memcpy steps (compiler-lowered strcpy/strcat idiom,
// not unresolved option semantics):
//   1. "SOFTWARE\\" literal                (*g_zGame_Options_RegKeyVersionSegment @ 0x4e4668)
//   2. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyRoot        (0x56bcd8, strdup'd by Options_InitRegistryContext)
//   3. + "\\" literal                       (at 0x4e4678)
//   4. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyCurrentUser (0x56bcdc)

//   6. + g_zGame_Options_RegKeyGame        (0x56bce0)

//
// --- KEY CREATION ---

//   [ebp-0x8] = HKLM handle  <- RegCreateKeyExA(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE =0x80000002)
//   [ebp-0xc] = lpdwDisposition (shared, result discarded)
//
// If HKCU create fails: closes [ebp-0x4] (invalid handle -- matches source
// binary behaviour; RegCloseKey on the zero-filled cell is a no-op/harmless
// on NT) and returns 0.
// If HKLM create fails: closes BOTH keys and returns 0.
//
// --- ENTRY WALK ---
// For each entry on g_zGame_Options_OptionListHead (->next at +0x18):
//   registryScope := entry->registryScope (+0x14)

// Opens a ZBD archive, sorts the manager's registered section handlers,
// and drives each handler's PreLoad callback so every handler can prepare
// its in-memory state from the index archive contents.
//
// --- CALLING CONVENTION ---
// __thiscall: ecx = zZbdManager* self, stack = char* filename.
// `retn 0x4` cleans up the 1 stack arg. Returns 0 on any failure, 1 on
// full success.
//
// --- STRUCT FIELD LAYOUT CONFIRMED ---
// struct zZbdManager (partial):
//   +0x04  zZbdSectionHandlerNode* sectionHandlerListSentinel
//          (ring-linked via Node::next at +0x0, Node::prev at +0x4,
//           Node::sectionHandler payload at +0x8)
//   +0x0c  zIndexArchive  archive              (embedded, NOT pointer)
//
// --- FLOW ---
// 1. Open/create the backing archive: zIndexArchive::OpenCreateWrite(
//      &self->archive, filename). Returns truthy on success, 0 on failure.
//    - On failure: ebx (i) stays 0, jump past the handler walk, return 0.
//    - On success: set ebx = 1 and continue.
//
// 2. Sort the section-handler list in ascending sortOrder:
//      zZbdManager::SortSectionHandlers(self)   (0x4c07d0)
//    This guarantees deterministic handler ordering during the preload
//    fan-out so later handlers can rely on earlier handlers' state.
//
// 3. Iterate the sorted handler ring (while node != sentinel AND i != 0):
//      Build stack context `ctx = { zZbdManager* mgr=self,
//                                   zZbdSectionHandler* handler=&node->sectionHandler }`
//      Invoke: zZbdSectionHandler::InvokePreLoad(
//                 &node->sectionHandler,   // ecx (this)
//                 &ctx)                    // stack arg
//      i = return value (0 = abort, non-zero = continue).
//      node = node->next.
//    Loop exits when either the ring is fully traversed or a handler
//    returned 0 (PreLoad veto).
//
// 4. Always close the archive:
//      zIndexArchive::CloseAndFreeRecords(&self->archive)
//    Runs on both success and handler-veto paths; only skipped when
//    OpenCreateWrite itself failed in step 1 (nothing to close).
//
// 5. Return i (ebx): 1 on full load success, 0 on open failure or handler
//    veto.
//
// --- SBB IDIOM NOTE ---
// The two pointer-equality checks at 0x4c03a1 and 0x4c03d1 are rendered
// by BN as `sete / neg / sbb / inc / test`. Both reduce to `node !=
// self->sectionHandlerListSentinel` -- the standard end-of-list guard
// for the ring walker.
//
// --- CALLERS ---
//   0x4c003c  zUtil_ZBD_LoadEntriesGlobal  -- thin null-guarded wrapper
//             around the process-wide g_zUtil_ZbdManager (0x56bf70).
//
// LIKELY SOURCE: zZbdManager::LoadEntries() in

// section-handler list. Destructively sorts all nodes from
